params.body:
Nightwatch issue 17: twice within a quarter of an hour, `simplexml_load_string()` threw a parse error while a dealer requested a Car-Pass and the vehicle therefore went back out to Nederland Mobiel. The dealer noticed nothing, the sheet saved — and nowhere was there any record of what Nederland Mobiel had actually said.

That is the shape of the problem. Webhooks have left a trail since `webhook_deliveries`; the feeds we push ourselves left none. What came back lived in one column on the vehicle row (`last_nederland_mobiel_response`), overwritten by the next attempt, readable only by opening that one vehicle. A refusal was invisible unless someone happened to look at exactly the right car.

**The answer is kept now.** The door reads the HTTP status and parses the answer itself under `libxml_use_internal_errors`, so an error page is an answer we store rather than a warning PHP turns into an exception with nothing in it. The message names the status and the first two hundred characters: "Nederland Mobiel antwoordde met HTTP 502 en geen XML: ...".

**Every call leaves one light row** in `partner_deliveries`: partner, vehicle, what we asked, status, whether the answer was usable, how long it took, and the start of what came back. Same shape and same rules as `webhook_deliveries` — only the answer, no foreign keys, pruned to thirty days by the daily `model:prune`. Written at the door itself, so the observer, the console command and a retry by hand all leave a row. Writing that row can never be the reason a call fails: if it cannot be written it goes to the log and the call carries on, and that is pinned by a test that pulls the database out from under the model.

**Beheer > Werking shows it**: per partner the calls of the last seven days, how many were refused, when the last one was, and the last five refusals with their reason. A refusal also reaches the attention layer at the top, because that is the only place it gets noticed without anyone opening a vehicle.

**One thing found along the way.** The call carried `CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 0`, which for cURL means "wait forever": a partner that stopped answering held the dealer's save until PHP gave up on its own. That is thirty seconds now.

New chapter P3-15 with three rules. `ARefusalFromAPartnerIsVisibleTest` covers the row, the excerpt cut, the write guard, the screen figures and the attention line; `OperationsScreenTest` gets the refusal on the screen with its reason. The PHPStan baseline is one entry shorter: the old `$apikey != '' && $apikey != null` is gone.

Fixes bevinding een-weigering-van-nederland-mobiel-is-onzichtbaar.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
params.title: A refusal from a partner is visible
